reasoning: Both implement the rules and handle timing well. A passes every tool check and types the per-player table as optional. B has two luau-lsp type errors in its own code, because it uses the loop variable from BlockTypes.Order as a BlockType without the cast. B also types the per-player table as always present, names its yielding loader without Async, and breaks project conventions. B's runtime block-type check is a nice touch, but A is the one ready to merge.

criteria.note: Loads from DATA_STORE_NAME "BlockInventory" with key `player_{UserId}`, buildCounts falls back to STARTING_COUNT 20, TakeBlock stops at 0, ReturnBlock stops at MAX_COUNT 99, GrantBlocks has no cap, GetCount reads a count, and onPlayerRemoving drops the player's counts.

The loadingPlayers flag throws away a load that finishes after the player left, functions return "NotLoaded" or nil for unloaded players, existing players are loaded with task.spawn, and requiring the module never yields.
Returns (false, "OutOfBlocks"/"AtLimit"/"NotLoaded"), only calls error() for a non-positive amount in GrantBlocks, and wraps GetDataStore and GetAsync in pcall.
Every public function has typed parameters and returns, uses BlockTypes.BlockType, types the per-player table as `{ [Player]: Counts? }`, and has per-function failure-reason unions.
GrantBlocks is a separate function for going past the cap, names are spelled out, and the yielding loader is named loadCountsAsync.
One module, no remotes or saving, BlockTypes reused, and all lint, format and type checks pass (the DataStore-name check is a false negative because the name is in a constant).
Same rules are implemented correctly: "BlockInventory" store, `player_{UserId}` key, defaults of 20, take stops at 0, returnBlock stops at 99 with "Full", and grantBlocks is uncapped.
The loadingPlayers guard, the duplicate-load guard, task.spawn for existing players, and "NotLoaded" failures cover the timing cases.
A FailureReason union including InvalidBlockType and InvalidAmount is returned as values, and the load is wrapped in pcall.
Uses the BlockType set, but countsByPlayer is `{ [Player]: Counts }` (not optional), and the missing loop-variable cast causes luau-lsp errors at lines 49 and 65.
grantBlocks is separate and names are clear, but the yielding loader is named `loadCounts` without Async.
luau-lsp reports two type errors in its own code, and it uses an instance-path require and local instead of const, against the project conventions.

strengths: Clean strict typing with the cast workaround and an optional per-player table value
Correct handling of a player leaving while their load is in flight, plus loading of players already in the server
Failure reasons tailored to each function
weaknesses: Doesn't check the block type at runtime even though values come from a remote
Method-call syntax (Module:TakeBlock) on a stateless table is a bit unusual

strengths: Checks the block type at runtime for input coming from a client
Guards against loading the same player twice and exposes an isLoaded helper
weaknesses: Fails luau-lsp in its own code (missing BlockType cast)
The per-player table type isn't optional
Doesn't follow conventions (instance-path require, local services, table not named Module)
